Convert a Word document to PDF

Source: R/pdf.R
docx_to_pdf.Rd

Converts a .docx file to PDF with LibreOffice, or with Microsoft Word through the doconv package. LibreOffice is free and runs on all platforms. Each call uses a fresh temporary LibreOffice profile, so it works while a LibreOffice window is open and in parallel runs.

Usage

docx_to_pdf(
  docx,
  pdf = NULL,
  engine = c("auto", "libreoffice", "word"),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  fonts = NULL
)

Arguments

docx

Path to an existing .docx file.

pdf

Path of the PDF to write. NULL (default) uses the path of docx with the extension changed to .pdf.

engine

"auto" (default) tries LibreOffice, then Word through doconv if that package is installed. "libreoffice" and "word" force one engine.

overwrite

Overwrite an existing pdf? Default FALSE.

verbose

Print progress messages? Default TRUE.

fonts

Font files (.ttf, .otf, .ttc) or folders of font files that LibreOffice should use for this conversion, in addition to the fonts it finds itself. Use it when a script shows as blank text or boxes in the PDF although the font is on the machine. NULL (default) uses the option convertxlsform.fonts, if set. Ignored by the Word engine.

Value

The path of the PDF, invisibly.

Details

If LibreOffice is installed in an unusual place, set the option convertxlsform.soffice or the environment variable CONVERTXLSFORM_SOFFICE to the path of the soffice binary.

Examples

if (interactive() && has_libreoffice()) {
  docx <- tempfile(fileext = ".docx")
  doc <- officer::read_docx()
  doc <- officer::body_add_par(doc, "Hello")
  print(doc, target = docx)
  pdf <- docx_to_pdf(docx, pdf = tempfile(fileext = ".pdf"))
  file.exists(pdf)
}
